FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Hosiery 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textiles Division Council. 

The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 


‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17776 : 2021 


Indian Standard 


TEXTILES — KNITTED COMBAT 
T-SHIRT — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard covers the requirement of cotton and 
polyester combat t-shirt in half sleeves round neck with 
disruptive pattern. 


1.2 This standard does not specify the general appearance, 
lustre, feel and shade of the combat t-shirt (see also 6). 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given in Annex A contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute provisions 
of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision 
and parties to agreements based on this standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying 
the most recent editions of the standards indicated in 
Annex A. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in 
IS 3596 shall apply. 


4 MATERIAL AND MANUFACTURE 


4.1 Fabric 


4.1.1 The base fabric of cotton combat t-shirt shall be 
plain interlock knitted cotton fabric manufactured from 
100 percent cotton, 40° Ne combed yarn conforming to IS 
834. The construction requirements of interlock knitted 
cotton fabric shall conform to designation medium ‘C’ 
as specified in Table 1 of IS 13003. The fabric shall be 
knitted on circular knitting machine with single yarn. 


4.1.2 The polyester combat t-shirt shall be manufactured 
from 100 percent polyester draw textured filament yarn 
knitted on circular knitting machine in interlock structure. 
The interlock fabric shall have plain and bird eye dot knit 
design at back and front (face) side respectively for gentle 
, good permeability and quick drying property. The face 
side of fabric shall be printed with disperse dye as per 
sealed pattern agreed between the buyer and the seller. 


4.2 Neck Band 


The neck band shall be in 1 x 1 rib knit. The yarn used for 
knitting the neck band shall be same as that of yarn used 
in body fabric and will be dyed in the same shade as of 
base colour of the combat t -shirt. The neck band, sleeve 
width, and bottom hem shall be 2.5 cm. 


4.3 Dye and Print 


The fabric shall be dyed with vat dye for cotton and with 
disperse dye for polyester. The fabric shall be printed 
with disruptive patterns as per the agreement between 
the buyer and the seller. The logo may be printed on left 
side of the chest in golden colour in design and size as 
per the agreement between the buyer and the seller. The 
print shall be durable enough to meet the colourfastness 
requirement as the specified in this standard. 


4.4 Seams and Stitches 


4.4.1 For stitching various portions of combat t-shirt, the 
type of stitches and count of sewing thread used shall 
be as given in Table 1. The sewing thread shall conform 
to IS 1720. In case of dyed/printed combat t-shirt the 
sewing thread should be of matching shade. 


4.4.2 The sleeve and bottom hem of combat t-shirt shall 
be stitched with double needle machine for cleaner, better 
finish and durability. All the seams shall be reinforced 
with over lock, stitched neatly as per sealed sample. 


4.4.3 The number of stitches shall not be less than 
AO stitches/dm. 


4.5 Reinforcement 


The neckline and shoulders of combat t-shirt shall be 
suitably reinforced with self-material forming tape and 
elastic tape respectively as that of sealed sample for 
better durability, comfort and fittings. 


4.6 Freedom from Defects 


The combat t-shirt shall be free from noticeable fabric 
defects such as mends, ladders, dropped/missed, tuck 
stitches, cut or tear, chemical damages, dyeing and 
printing defects, such as bare, streaky, uneven, hazy 
dyeing and misprinting. The combat t-shirt shall also 
free from garment fabrication defects such as improper 
reinforcement, missed, loose, uneven stitches, badly 
sewn, misalignments of components and any other 
defects which significantly affect the appearance or 
serviceability of the garment. 


5 DESIGN, SHAPE AND DIMENSION 


5.1 The combat T-Shirt shall be manufactured with 
round neck in half sleeves to the shape, dimension and 
design as given in Table 2, Fig 1 and Fig 2. The combat 
t-shirt may also be manufactured in other shape, 
dimension and design per the agreement between the 
buyer and the seller.

IS 17776 : 2021 


6 SEALED SAMPLE 


6.1 If in order to illustrate or specify the indeterminable 
characteristics, such as general appearance, lustre, feel 
and colour of combat t-shirt, a sample has been agreed 
upon and sealed, the supply shall be in conformity with 
the sample in such respects. 


6.2 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a matter 
of prior agreement between the buyers and the sellers. 


7 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENT 


7.1 The combat t-shirt shall confirm to the requirement 
as specified in Table 3. 


8 MARKING 


8.1 A suitable cloth label made of woven cotton, taffeta/ 
satin or fusing type shall be fastened or fused to combat 
t-shirt at the inside of the neck portion on which the 
following shall be indicated by printing: 


a) Size; 


b) Manufacturer’s name or recognized trade mark; 
c) Batch No. /Lot No and date of manufacturing; 
d) Count of yarn, fibre composition and GSM; 


e) Wash Care label; 


f) Country of manufacture; and 


g) Any other information required by the buyer or 


the law in force. 


NOTE — The colour from the label shall not bleed on to the 


combat t-shirt during storage or use.

8.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


9 PACKING 


The combat t-shirt shall be packed individually in 
self-sealing polythene bags with recycled cardboard 
300 GSM of suitable size and ten t-shirts be tied 
into a bundle and further packed in bales or cases in 
accordance with IS 3325 or IS 3086 as the case may be. 


10 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY 


10.1 The sampling procedure detailed in 10.2 to 10.3 
shall give desired protection to the buyer and the 
seller provided the lot submitted for inspection is 
homogeneous. To achieve this, the manufacturers shall 
maintain system of process control at all stages of 
manufacture ensuring that combat t-shirt tendered by 
him for inspection comply with the requirements of this 
standard in all respects. 

NOTE — For effective process control, the use of statistical 

quality control technique is recommended and helpful 

guidance may be obtained in this respect from IS 397 (Part 1) 


10.2 In any consignment all the combat t-shirt of the 
same size and manufactured from the same count and 


IS 17776 : 2021 


quality of yarn and delivered to a buyer against one 
despatch note shall constitute a lot. 


10.2.1 The conformity of a lot to the requirements of 
this specification shall be determined on the basis of 
the tests carried out on the samples selected from the 
lot. These combat t-shirts shall be selected at random 
from the lot. For this purpose, reference may be made 
to IS 4905. 


10.3 All the combat t-shirt selected as per column 3 
of Table 4 shall be examined for visual inspection, 
dimension, freedom from defect etc. Any combat t-shirt 
failing in one or more of the above requirements shall 
be termed as defective. The lot shall be considered 
as conforming to the above requirements, if the total 
number of defectives found in the sample is less than 
or equal to the acceptance number given in column 4 of 
Table 4. Otherwise, the lot shall be rejected. 


10.3.1 If the samples are found satisfactory according 
to 10.3, samples will be drawn as per column 5 of Table 
4 for physical testing, from the sample originally drawn 
as per column 3 of Table 4. 


10.3.2. For chemical parameters sample to be drawn as 
per column 7 of Table 4 randomly from the samples as 
per column 5 of Table 4. 


10.3.3 Acceptance no. mentioned in the physical 
parameter column 6 of Table 4 is inclusive of chemical 
parameter column 8 of Table 4 that is total acceptance 
number should not exceed acceptance number 
mentioned in column 6 of Table 4.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
